facts.raw_span: A 65-year-old man
hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and bronchial asthma
mild headaches of several months’ duration
no focal neurologic deficits
Laboratory studies were normal
Noncontrast CT of the head revealed a well-defined, 19-mm mass in the left parietal bone
sparse but preserved trabeculae and a slight bony bulge, without disruption of the inner or outer tables
MRI showed the lesion to be isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images
multiple internal hyperintense foci, heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted images, and restricted diffusion
the hyperintense foci on T1 images were presumed to represent bone marrow fat
the preserved trabecular architecture suggested that pre-existing structures were not destroyed
no significant change in the identified lesion since then

concepts.why: The patient has a well-defined, 19-mm mass in the left parietal bone with sparse but preserved trabeculae and a slight bony bulge, which is consistent with an osteoma.
The patient has a bone mass with multiple internal hyperintense foci on T1-weighted images, which could represent a hemangioma of bone.
The patient has a bone mass with preserved trabecular architecture, which could be consistent with fibrous dysplasia.
The patient has headaches and a mass in the left parietal bone, which could be a meningioma.
The patient has headaches and a history of a stable lesion, which could be a chronic subdural hematoma.
The patient has hypertension, which increases the risk of hypertensive heart disease.
The patient has diabetes mellitus, which increases the risk of diabetic neuropathy.
The patient has bronchial asthma, which is a chronic respiratory condition.
The lesion's isointensity to muscle on T1-weighted images and presence of internal hyperintense foci representing bone marrow fat are consistent with intraosseous hemangioma.
